questions.question: Which statements about elicitation are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Form mode collects structured data against a schema the client uses to build and validate an input form
URL mode sends the user to a URL out of band, suitable for credentials and third-party OAuth
Servers must not use form mode for passwords, API keys, tokens, or payment credentials
The server delivers elicitation/create as a direct server-initiated request over a reverse channel in 2026-07-28
Users may decline or cancel an elicitation

questions.explanation: All are true except D: under 2026-07-28, elicitation rides the MRTR pattern — the server returns an InputRequiredResult and the client retries the original request with inputResponses; server-initiated requests are gone.

questions.question: Which client-side features are deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Sampling
Roots
Elicitation
Protocol-level logging via notifications/message
Tools

questions.explanation: SEP-2577 deprecates Roots, Sampling, and Logging. Elicitation remains active (now via MRTR), and tools are a core server primitive.

questions.question: For URL-mode elicitation, which client behaviors does the specification require or describe? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Show the full URL to the user
Gather explicit consent before opening the URL
Never fetch the URL automatically
Capture the data the user enters on the target site and return it to the server
Learn only whether the user consented

questions.explanation: URL mode exists precisely so the data stays out of band: the client shows the URL, gets consent, never auto-fetches, and learns only the consent outcome. Capturing the entered data would defeat the mode's purpose.

questions.question: Which fields belonged to the (deprecated) sampling request's modelPreferences? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: hints — suggested model names
costPriority
speedPriority
intelligencePriority
gpuMemoryLimit

questions.explanation: modelPreferences carried model hints plus three 0–1 priorities (cost, speed, intelligence) guiding the client's model selection. There is no GPU field.

questions.question: In the MRTR pattern, which elements appear in the flow? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The server returns an InputRequiredResult with resultType: "input_required"
The inputRequests field carries the elicitations or other requests needing answers
The client retries the ORIGINAL request, attaching inputResponses keyed to the requests
The server-echoed requestState rides along so any stateless instance can resume the work
The client MUST send a new tools/call for each inputRequest in parallel

questions.explanation: That is the complete MRTR loop (SEP-2322): interim result → client gathers input → retry with inputResponses + requestState. All statements hold.

questions.question: Which data may a server legitimately collect via FORM-mode elicitation? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A project name (string with a description)
A priority level (enum of low/medium/high)
A boolean confirmation
The user's GitHub personal access token
All of the above

questions.explanation: Form mode is for ordinary structured data. Credentials — passwords, API keys, tokens, payment details — must never go through form mode; that's what URL mode exists for.

questions.question: Which migrations does the changelog suggest for the features deprecated by SEP-2577? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Roots → pass directories/files via tool parameters, resource URIs, or server configuration
Sampling → integrate directly with LLM provider APIs
Logging → log to stderr (stdio) or use OpenTelemetry
Roots → replace with the ping method
All of the above

questions.explanation: A–C are the documented migration paths. ping was itself removed in 2026-07-28, so D is doubly wrong.

questions.question: Why did 2026-07-28 remove notifications/elicitation/complete and the elicitationId field? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Under MRTR, the client learns the outcome by retrying the original request, so a server-initiated completion signal no longer fits
Server-to-client requests outside a request's response no longer exist in the stateless model
Servers needing to correlate an elicitation across retries encode their own identifier in requestState
Elicitation as a whole was removed from the protocol
All of the above

questions.explanation: Elicitation survives — only its 2025-11-25 completion-notification plumbing went away, replaced by the MRTR retry loop. D is the snuck-in falsehood.
